heroHeadline: Sudan Deploys Troops to Ethiopian Border as Khartoum Airport Closure Enters Day 4; UN and UK Condemn RSF Drone Attacks
heroSubtitle: On Day 1119, Sudan reinforced its eastern border with ground troops and anti-aircraft systems deployed to East Gallabat, Basunda, and the disputed Al-Fashaga zone in Gedaref State — the first confirmed conventional SAF border buildup in direct response to Khartoum's accusation that Ethiopia allowed RSF drones to be launched from Bahir Dar Airport against Sudanese sovereign territory. Khartoum International Airport remained closed for a fourth day as Sudan's Prime Minister visited the site to assess damage. The United Nations and the United Kingdom formally condemned the RSF drone attacks on the airport. Sudan's ambassador remained recalled from Addis Ababa with no timeline for return; Ethiopia continued to reject Sudan's accusations as 'baseless.' An Al Jazeera analytical report published May 8 projected that if Sudan's civil war continues to 2030, cumulative GDP losses will reach $34.5 billion and an additional 34 million people will be pushed into extreme poverty — on top of the 28.9 million already acutely food insecure. All diplomatic efforts remain deadlocked, with no active ceasefire talks and the Quad's humanitarian truce proposal (US, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, UAE) still blocked by fundamental disagreements on sequencing. Sudan has now entered its fourth year of civil war with approximately 14 million displaced, 150,000+ killed, and 34 million in urgent need of humanitarian support.
